doc.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996

title: Recording sessions with McShann and Basie
summary: Albums were made in about six hours with two or three microphones; two-track recording was best.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: That’s exciting. Yeah. That’s great. When you first started recording with Jay McShann, what was a record session like compared to these days. Did you go in and kind of do the whole album and —
We’d do the whole album in about six hours. Three hours one day, three hours the next day. That’s it. Probably two microphones.
One for you and one for the band.
One for the band. And one for Jay. About three.
And with Count Basie, and do you know what? Two tracks still. It’s the best form of recording. Two tracks. Of course you’ve got everybody there.
And they’re listening to each other.
They are listening to each other.
